title: Intel Processors Explained (Official Dell Tech Support)
description: Understand processor differences for Intel's Core i3, i5, and i7.  Intel processors explained explores the features of each to help you decide which is best for you.  For more information please visit http://dell.com/support For support questions email us at [EMAIL]

asr.full_text: Welcome to Dell Tech Support. The processor is the computer's engine, and there are many different types, each of. Them with slightly different performance. In this video we'll go over some of the main features of Intel's 7th generation of. Processors. The speed at which your system runs programs, loads pages, and downloads files depends in. Part on the processor. Bandwidth, clock speed, and the number of cores in the processor all help determine. Processor performance. Generally speaking, a higher core number indicates higher speed when comparing the same type of processor. For example, a Core i7 will perform faster than a Core i3,. And the latest generation will have the most improved performance. So the 7th generation can deliver more features such as power and battery life than its predecessors. Here's a quick rundown of the key features. The Intel Core i3 processors have incredible battery life and smooth streaming. They have fantastic HD entertainment with full-screen 4K and 360 viewing, impeccable visuals, immersive entertainment, and effortless multitasking. They also have powerful performance and seamless computing at home and on the go. Intel Core i5 processors feature Intel Turbo Boost Technology 2.0, full-screen 4K and 360 viewing, and have lightning-fast startup times, as well as longer-lasting battery life and faster recharging. The Intel Core i7 processor is equipped with Intel Turbo Boost Technology 2.0. It also has. Smooth streaming and HD Entertainment enabled immersion full-screen 4k and 360 experience. In addition it has lightning speed data transfer of Thunderbolt 3. So what does all this really. Mean to you? Well that depends on what you plan on using your computer for. For regular home use,. Like browsing the web, streaming music and videos, playing simple games, i3 is enough. If you need a computer for multitasking, working on spreadsheets while streaming,. Editing photos or making home videos, and gaming, i5 is a better choice. For more advanced use and more power, as in creating complex animation,. 3D modeling, high-resolution video, i7 is probably your best bet. If you have questions or need additional help, contact us through our social media support on Facebook or Twitter and a Dell Tech Expert will be happy to assist you. Thanks for watching, and if you liked this video, give us a like, and be sure to subscribe to our channel.
